items.title: Remembering Uncommemorated Genocides & Holocausts
items.subtitle: A sub-archive within The Anarchive
items.abstract: A dedicated sub-archive within The GSS Anarchive: interactive data anarchives of the genocides, holocausts, and structural atrocities that mainstream memory refuses to keep. Curated from the research of Dr. Gideon Polya and other dissenting scholars, and hand-authored GSS counter-archives. Six entries now open: the Muslim Holocaust / Muslim Genocide (post-9/11, 32M avoidable deaths across 20 countries); the Aboriginal Genocide in Australia (1788 to present, ongoing); The Unwritten Ledger (caste, atrocity and the record in the Indian subcontinent); The ISN Registry (Guantánamo Bay, 780 numbers, 24 years); The Paper Trail (Abu Ghraib and the chain of authorisation); and The Manifest (Balochistan, extraction and the disappeared). Every entry is a full data page with chapters, charts, timelines, voices, and sources.

items.title: The Manifest
items.subtitle: Balochistan · Extraction, Disappearance & the Arithmetic That Will Not Close
items.abstract: GSS Anarchive · Collection 08. A counter-archive of Balochistan — 44% of Pakistan's landmass, holder of its gas, its copper, its deep-water port — built as a shipping manifest. What leaves (Sui gas piped to Punjab from 1952, Reko Diq copper and gold, Gwadar's CPEC concession), what arrives (internment centres, the 2025 Anti-Terrorism (Balochistan) Amendment Section 11-EEEE, anti-terrorism courts sitting inside Hudda Jail), and the one category that appears on no manifest at all: the disappeared. Voice for Baloch Missing Persons and Paank vs. Pakistan's own Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances — three counts of a number that will not close. Design conceit: the freight document; Baloch doch embroidery lattice at the threshold of visibility.

items.title: The ISN Registry
items.subtitle: Guantánamo & the Manufacture of Lawlessness
items.abstract: GSS Anarchive · Collection 05. On arrival at Guantánamo Bay a man stopped being a name and became an Internment Serial Number. This counter-archive adopts that unit and turns it against itself: 780 marks, one per person ever held, arranged as a wall; ten registry files indexed by ISN; a twenty-four year chronology; a five-part legal-architecture diagram (the Lease, the Category, the Number, the Commission, the Ban on Exit). Names are put back beside numbers. Design conceit: the number is the archival unit — adopted in order to be broken. Refuses trophy imagery and torture-derived statements. Fifteen men remain inside as the page is served.

items.title: The Paper Trail
items.subtitle: Abu Ghraib & the Chain of Authorisation
items.abstract: GSS Anarchive · Collection 06. Abu Ghraib is filed in public memory as a photography scandal. It was a paperwork scandal. This counter-archive contains no photographs and follows the memoranda instead — twelve documents in a chain of authorisation from the 2002 Bybee memo through Rumsfeld's December 2002 signature and the 'GTMOization' of Iraq in August 2003, into the hard site at Tier 1A, out through the Taguba report and the 2004 broadcast, and ending in the 2026 Fourth Circuit affirmance of Al Shimari v. CACI. Design conceit: the memo, not the photograph — the signature device is a redaction bar the reader must lift by hand. Includes an accountability-by-rank ladder (Cabinet: no charges → enlisted: prison), nine case files, and standing ethical rules.

items.title: Planetary Justice Map
items.subtitle: Gendered Networks of Revolutionary Solidarity
items.abstract: An interactive research map of radical solidarities across borders: seven revolutionary figures and three movements of the Global Souths, their trajectories and documented ties. Node dossiers pair factual annotations with labelled interpretive readings, 29 coded primary materials (photographs, speeches, writings — linked at their holding archives), a century timeline, a coordinate gazetteer, and Chicago/BibTeX citation export. Research design: Bibhushana Poudyal. Open source, built on MapLibre GL.

items.title: The Unwritten Ledger
items.subtitle: Caste, Atrocity & the Record — a counter-archive of the Indian subcontinent
items.abstract: GSS Anarchive · Collection 04. A counter-archive of caste, atrocity and refusal in the Indian subcontinent — organized as a double-entry ledger between what the state enters in the register and what the register cannot hold. Follows the FIR that was never filed, the atrocity where the court found 'no caste motive,' the assembly ballot Ambedkar named for what it was, and the Buddhist conversion of October 1956 — twelve files, keyed to the ruled line of a state ledger. Design conceit: two columns — Ambedkarite blue for the recorded claim, gold for the unrecorded testimony.

items.title: The Aboriginal Genocide in Australia
items.subtitle: 1788 to the present — Frontier Wars, Stolen Generations, ongoing avoidable death
items.abstract: An interactive data anarchive of the ongoing Aboriginal Genocide in Australia — from the 1788 invasion and the 19th-century Frontier Wars, through the Stolen Generations (100,000 children forcibly removed), to today's ~4,000 avoidable Indigenous deaths per year and the 11.5-year life-expectancy gap. Includes population-collapse visualization (350k–1M → 100k → 670k), a chronological timeline, the UN Genocide Convention framework with all five acts marked as applying, a side-by-side comparison with the Palestinian Genocide, and period quotes from the perpetrators. Figures are Dr. Gideon Polya's documented avoidable-mortality estimates, presented faithfully with full attribution.

items.title: The Muslim Holocaust, Muslim Genocide
items.subtitle: An interactive data anarchive of post-9/11 avoidable mortality
items.abstract: An interactive data visualization of Dr. Gideon Polya's research on the US-imposed post-9/11 Muslim Holocaust and Muslim Genocide — 32 million avoidable Muslim deaths across 20 countries (5 million from violence, 27 million from war-imposed deprivation). Features a live world map of avoidable death by nation, animated charts of mortality, refugee displacement, the colonial-era ledger (1950–2005), a chronology of interventions, the UN Genocide Convention standard, and Polya's climate-genocide projection. Figures are the author's documented avoidable-mortality estimates, presented faithfully with full attribution.
